text: We need the collective efforts of the whole of society, by which I mean employers, co-workers, community organisations and businesses, all being supportive in words and deeds.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ultimately, people now marry and have kids because they want to, not because they have to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This being the case, it is my belief that there are three important elements that help individuals decide in favour of marriage and parenthood and, that is, when they feel that marriage and parenthood are achievable, enjoyable and celebrated.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: First, ensuring that marriage and parenthood are achievable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I find the strong sense of responsibility among young Singaporeans that was admirable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They want to have stable jobs and build up some financial resources before settling down.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our unemployment rate has been among the lowest in the world, consistently.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Employment levels are high across all age groups.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Income growth may have moderated as our economy matures, but it is still positive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the efforts we are making to restructure industries and update skills, good jobs and income growth remain within reach, including for future generations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A second important factor for young Singaporeans is home ownership.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thankfully, we have an extensive public housing programme that has kept home ownership affordable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Many young couples are able to own their first marital homes through the BTO programme, something unheard of in most cities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is a great help to family finances.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Saktiandi Supaat have asked if we could shorten the average waiting time for BTO flats.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: HDB builds flats ahead of orders, but in a measured way.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government understands Singaporeans' aspirations for home ownership and MND will continue to focus on helping young couples own their first home.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: HDB also introduced PPHS in 2013 for couples waiting for their flats to be completed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: PPHS offers HDB flats at below market rental rates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The PPHS rental homes were the first homes for 270 babies!

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: PPHS flats have been offered in a range of mature and non-mature estates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Currently, we have about 150 PPHS flats available for application in Tiong Bahru and Jurong.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thus far, the supply of PPHS flats has been sufficient to meet demand and we will continue to monitor the take-up rate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are also measures to help families live closer to one another for caregiving support, a point Mr Louis Ng raised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The priority for BTO housing to couples who want to live with or near to their parents has also been offered.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And we saw in the papers today that more than 2,000 families have benefited from the Proximity Housing Grant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another key factor is quality childcare that is accessible and affordable, as noted by Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Leon Perera.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Parents want to have peace of mind knowing that their children are well looked after while they work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They also want their children to socialise and learn.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MSF, the Early Childhood Development Agency and the Ministry of Education (MOE) have been working jointly to increase childcare provision.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There will be 10,000 more by the end of next year, especially in the newer estates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will help to improve accessibility and make it closer to homes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About 30% of childcare centres are also located near workplaces.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Childcare subsidies are available to all parents and additional means-tested subsidies are available to help lower- and middle-income families with childcare costs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, there are gaps that we can plug.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, there are parents with infants who have no family support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: NPTD will study these ideas together with MSF.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our goal is to improve childcare provision so that all parents who need it can access and afford it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is the way for couples and even singles to see that their aspirations for parenthood are achievable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Much progress has been made and I know Minister Tan Chuan-Jin is fully committed to this goal.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Similarly, Minister Ng Chee Meng and Minister of State Dr Janil Puthucheary are also doing their best to support this effort in MOE.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Darryl David made important points about giving parents a sense of support throughout their parenting journeys.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In particular, we will give greater support to new parents in the year before and after the birth of their babies.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As a result, the majority of subsidised deliveries in public hospitals will have their bills fully covered by MediSave, including pre-delivery expenses.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Previously, parents had to first save into CDA to receive the dollar-for-dollar matching by the Government.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have introduced the CDA First Step to provide the first $3,000 into CDAs, without parents having to save first.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Parents who deposit savings into their children's CDAs will continue to enjoy dollar-for-dollar matching, up to the remaining Government contribution caps.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These two initiatives complement the other marriage and parenthood benefits like the Baby Bonus Cash Gift and parenthood tax rebates and reliefs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Education is of high quality and heavily subsidised, from primary to post-secondary and even tertiary levels.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: An increasing number of student care centres help address the caregiving needs of working parents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MOE has said that all primary schools will have student care centres by 2020, not so far away.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: More help is also provided to needy families, including through new measures like KidSTART and the Fresh Start housing scheme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Taken together, there is significant support for marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Members can see, there are many programmes and initiatives implemented by different agencies that support marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They show the Government's strong commitment to make Singapore a "Great Place for Families".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the additional efforts and resources we are putting in, I hope more Singaporeans will see that marriage and parenthood are achievable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As Ms Tin says, marriage, parenthood and career are not mutually exclusive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, all the above are necessary but probably insufficient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked what we can learn from the developed countries.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It has to do primarily with the lack of support by employers and co-workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are also unhelpful workplace practices and cultures, resulting in long hours away from home.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In Korea, there is a very strong sense of "presentee-ism", in other words, being present, and, especially not leaving work until your boss has done so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There is also a very prevalent culture of "hoesik".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It literally means "staff company dinner" but basically it means that after work, let us all go out and have a drink, socialise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But it takes time away from the family.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, these are workplace cultures that are not always helpful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak pointed out that child-raising costs continue to be a concern.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some have to do with the lack of family-support and, therefore, the need to pay for help; whereas previously you could always count on your wife who was not working, or mum, or mother-in-law, who would stay at home.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Parents opting to pay for more than the basics, in every respect.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It could also be due to the tendency to practise an intensive style of parenting which we see a lot of in Korea.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In Korea, the parents put a lot of resources in helping the child prepare for school and even prepare for what happens after school.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These contribute to making parenting more stressful and less enjoyable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the UK, childcare cost is actually not that low, but their TFR is good.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is something that Ms Sun Xueling observed, that targeting parents' cost concerns alone will not be sufficient.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another important lesson is that employers did not implement family-friendly practices purely out of altruism or charity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead, they saw these practices as a competitive advantage, necessary to attract and retain capable staff and helpful for productivity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, the Hertie Foundation in Berlin pioneered a work and family audit that is endorsed by the German government and adopted in Austria, Hungary and Italy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The audit findings indicate that family-friendly employers with scores in the top quartile had significantly better business outcomes than companies in the bottom quartile.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, in response to Mr Thomas Chua's comment, family-friendly practices may, in fact, complement efforts to improve productivity and we would like to see how this can be strengthened.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Germany's TFR is, however, not as high as the Nordic countries and France.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Researchers believe that it has to do with traditional expectations held in Germany until very recently, that is, that good mothers must stop work to care for their children.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This has made it harder for German women to enjoy both career and parenthood, even if they did not face discrimination at work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In contrast, women in the Nordic countries and France do not face similar pressures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can continue to pursue their career aspirations, which as Mr Saktiandi rightly pointed out, should also be the case in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I agree with Mr Saktiandi and Ms Tin that discrimination against pregnant women or parents is not acceptable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Beyond legislation, TAFEP has also stepped up efforts to promote fair, responsible and progressive employment practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I also agree with Ms Tin and Mr Desmond Choo that FWAs help employees better manage work and family commitments and, as a result, they make parenting a more enjoyable process.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The take-up of the Work-Life Grant is improving, but I do think more can be done.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We support Mr Choo's suggestion, in particular, to work with the tripartite partners to explore how FWAs can be promoted in a more targeted manner in different sectors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We should also support and show understanding towards nursing mothers, a point Mr Alex Yam has made.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is much lower than in other developed societies, including Australia, which has it at 18%, South Korea, 11% and Taiwan, a whopping 50%.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During my focus group discussions with parents, many shared that they would like greater employer and community support for breastfeeding.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One enlightened local company Yang Kee Logistics is a good example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Breastfeeding mothers enjoy the privacy of a nursing room.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Employees can also use a specially designed Children's Corner if they need to take the children to work, for example, when the childcare centre is closed for the day.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ahead of legislation, fathers who are working in Yang Kee Logistics already enjoy two weeks of paternity leave and an extra two days to spend more time with their newborns.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mind you, Yang Kee is not a big company.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When parents feel supported by their employers and co-workers, they tend to enjoy parenthood more and, therefore, be more motivated to have more children.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Their single colleagues, too, take the cue and will likely be more favourable towards marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The wider community, too, plays an important role.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Alex Yam shared his difficulties about changing diapers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, we hope that there will be more developers of shopping malls and commercial buildings who will improve facilities for parents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They can take advantage of BCA's Accessibility Fund which provides 40% of the construction costs of family-friendly features.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But after they build these facilities, I agree with Mr Yam that the buildings must open them and let people use them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Saktiandi talked about the ease of travel on public transport for young parents and, indeed, the Land Transport Authority (LTA) introduced priority lanes which apply to pregnant women as well as families with children in strollers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I agree with him that we should do more in this area.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Sun Xueling suggested having more child-friendly community spaces and self-help community groups for parents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I recently came across an online support group called "Daddy Matters".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is all men, just young fathers, and the group told me that sometimes they "just need a listening ear and to share tips".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Indeed, parents' best coaches and confidantes are often other parents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I hope there will be more of such organic support groups.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: France, the UK and the Nordic countries all provide strong support for parents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Among them, as Mr Vikram Nair has pointed out, France has consistently had the highest TFR of nearly 2.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The UK, where childcare is actually less well organised and state support less generous than in the other countries, has a sustained TFR of 1.83.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is higher than the average TFR in Finland and Denmark, of about 1.7, where childcare is actually very well organised and fully supported.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For reasons that are not completely understood, it seems that there are other factors that influence TFR, such as historical, geographical and other socio-economic factors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another factor could be the way society values and celebrates families and children that make people want to have kids.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Respected sociologist and former Nominated Member, Prof Paulin Straughan, once observed that "no one is going to give you a prize for getting married and having kids!" She believes this explains why some people are not taking proactive steps to find a partner, settle down and start families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I, therefore, fully support calls by Ms Sun Xueling and Mr Alex Yam for a whole-of-society effort to foster positive mindsets towards marriage and parenthood and shaping supportive social norms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those of us who have had the privilege of being parents know how transformational the experience is.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are, indeed, many sacrifices parents make – sleep, personal time, freedom and stretch marks – to name a few.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But nothing quite compares to the joy of holding your own child, the knowledge that you gave life and the relationship with a precious human being.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And as Mr Alex Yam and Mr Darryl David have pointed out, fathers feel these emotions just as strongly as mothers do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we must, as a society, continue to celebrate parenthood, celebrate having babies and celebrate families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if you start now, there is good time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As with the current one week of shared parental leave, the four weeks will be shared from the mother's maternity leave.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the enhancements to paternity leave and shared parental leave, fathers will be able to take up to eight weeks of leave, about two months, in the baby's first year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will be effective for children adopted from 1 July 2017 onwards.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am aware that even as parents-to-be cheer these leave enhancements, some businesses, including SMEs, with higher concentrations of male staff may have concerns, as Mr Thomas Chua and Mr Desmond Choo have highlighted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, the Association of Small and Medium Enterprises has also shared concerns with us.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is also out of concerns for businesses and the employability of parents that we assess Mr Louis Ng's suggestion for extended childcare leave, or to peg a parent's childcare leave entitlement to the number of children, to be impractical for now.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have timed this round of leave enhancements to give employers some time to adjust and plan.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We hope employers who are in a position to do so will start to extend paternity leave even before legislation kicks in so that parents of children born earlier can also benefit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I shared earlier, the extra benefits should be thought of as important and powerful signals to their employees about their commitment towards family-friendly practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In English): Sir, this is the first time during the COS debate that I am wearing the NPTD hat.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have chosen to focus on two main aspects of our work: how we can promote marriage and parenthood so that we can grow the Singaporean Core from within; and how we keep Singapore cohesive and open, where Singaporeans feel connected and confident, as we supplement and expand the Core.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It starts with making sure that Singapore is a "Great Place for Families" so that marriage and parenthood are achievable, enjoyable and celebrated.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The continued story of Singapore and all of us who have chosen to make it our home is best described by former Deputy Prime Minister S Rajaratnam, when he said, "Being a Singaporean is not a matter of ancestry.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is conviction and choice." Our vision requires conviction and choice.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It will take all of our collective efforts to build on our Pioneers' legacy, to keep Singapore our best home – Cohesive and Open, and a Great Place for Families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I invite you to be a partner on this journey.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am very happy to note that engineers receive attention from our leaders.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And what is the age group, whether we are getting the young ones or is it a combination?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But I think as they progress, that is equally important.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, is there a review on the career path and the remuneration package?

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Mr Chairman, the recruitment will be over a range of experiences, a combination of all the things Er Dr Lee Bee Wah described.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Some will be beginning engineers, some will be experienced engineers.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: And some will be Singaporeans, but not all.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But I think it is also important that this is not just about salaries.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We want to develop their careers so that we have the types of engineers which we are all proud of.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier, the Minister mentioned that the Government has a robust framework in place to detect money laundering, including offences related to corruption.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He also mentioned STRO, which I think has been in place for quite a number of years.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: From what I know from investigations, you would only seize accounts if you have some prima facie grounds to suspect that there have been offences committed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister whether this may suggest that the framework in place may need a review because it may not really be robust enough for its purpose.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Any framework must be constantly reviewed and updated.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Whenever we receive any information, whether domestically or from our foreign sources, we will undertake the necessary investigation to get to the bottom of it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, this is how we do things in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Once we get any information, we will get to the bottom of it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Having done the investigation for the specific case, we will always follow up and ask ourselves is there a need for us to strengthen our framework.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, it is a continuous process and we will never let our guard down.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I will not be able to comment on any of the investigations because I think it is not correct for us to make any specific comments while investigations are ongoing.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I have two clarifications for the Deputy Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: One, the Deputy Prime Minister earlier mentioned the 400 over cases of harassment against Public Service officers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: If it was a physical presence, then is PSD also checking the virtual harassment 	vis-a-vis things like email, Facebook posting or letters that were sent?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: The public officer may feel there was a harassment to them as far as how they have conducted themselves fairly.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: These were cases which were reported to the Police.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, they would be the more serious cases.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: There might well have been harassment cases of other types, but perhaps not serious enough to be reported to the Police.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: As Mr Ang has correctly pointed out, if there are threats made to public officers, as we have seen in the media recently, where certain individuals have been taken to task and brought to Court because they were inciting the public to take matters into their own hands against certain Police officers and public officers, they will be taken to task even if that was done on the Internet.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: We will take these matters seriously, whether they are face-to-face or whether they are on the Internet, when incitement to violence against public officers is made.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: These are matters which we will take very seriously.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: The second question relates to whether we will do more to celebrate the courteous engagement between the two, rather than focusing only on harassment cases alone.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: It is not just courtesy but we also, at each Public Service Week, give awards to members of the public who have contributed to not just positive engagement but to helping the Public Service do their work well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Chairman, I was in a student forum recently and a student asked if having a technical engineering background will still allow him to aspire to a C-suite level job.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I found the question both telling and sad.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I personally think that the rise of technopreneurs will help to correct this trend.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I was wondering if the Minister could shed some light on what we can do further to change mindsets about engineering as a profession.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: You were asked about whether people can get to the C-suite.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Well, you can get to the M-suite if you are an engineer.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: There are quite a few in the front bench who are engineers.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I can cite a few examples of outstanding Singaporean corporate leaders who are engineers themselves.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: If you run a company or an organisation which requires technical competence in order to make it succeed and work, and you do not look after the financials and the marketing, you are not going to be able to sell your product no matter how good it is.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: On the other hand, if you have only financial people and marketing people and they ignore the need for a good product, then you can easily run the company to the ground.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, you do need a combination of both.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: So, I would say to a young engineer, "Press on, keep an open mind, make use of the skills that you have.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: With an engineering and technical background, you are equipped with many of the skills that you need to be successful in life."

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But I hope that in the near future, it will be reviewed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is really from feedback of residents who have about three kids, because the current two days of leave is really insufficient.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And I will join Members and fellow fathers in this House to declare that I have also changed my fair share of nappies.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am not sure that was a clarification, but are there any more?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Chairman, I would like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister who mentioned 	just now that not all the 1,000 engineers will be Singaporean.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Under what circumstances will you employ foreign engineers?

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: I think even Er Dr Lee would want to employ a person who can do the job best for your customer and, in this case, our customer is a Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: If there are areas in which we need expertise in order to execute public projects well, we will employ them.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: But clearly, we want to develop a strong engineering core in the Public Service in those areas which I have described.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: For that, we will train Singaporeans to be able to take leadership roles and build expertise in those areas.

speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
text: Also, they could well be immigrants who have joined the core and become Singaporeans, like yourself, Er Dr Lee.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This clarification is for Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: One of the big differences between France and many other countries is that they are traditional socialists in many ways and that includes education.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, they start from a very early age, preschool, I believe from the age of three or so, that is institutionalised care for children.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: How big a factor do you think that plays?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: On this particular issue, I will just plant my flag and say that when it comes to education, I do sit with the socialists.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think that that is one of the great equalisers.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Singapore has done well because from primary school onwards, there is a fairly level playing field.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But now, I think things start a bit earlier and, in preschool, there is a much greater diversity of services.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Do you think there is a role – I think right now, we have the anchor operators – for them to have a much larger share of the preschool market, so that more people will have access to it?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: We judge success by the number of people who take up preschool education as opposed to just a number of new centres that are set up.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, the aspiration should be: can we get all children enrolled, for example, in nursery or even earlier, if necessary?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Vikram Nair has asked a very interesting question.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, when we interacted with our French counterparts, one of the things that was very consistent, whether it was meeting with the policymakers in their MSF, MOE or CPF equivalent which is involved in the disbursements of the benefits, every single one of them, in giving us the background to France's policies when it came to childcare, mentioned the year 1945.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not understand French, but from the interpretation and the conversation, the year was significant for them because in 1945, the French state was brought to its knees as they lost so many citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There was a collective sense of urgency that has stayed with them to this day, that you need to reproduce, you need to have more of your own.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is exactly the same kind of mentality which Mr Thomas Chua described would have been needed for 西夏, that is, even though they were superior in their capabilities, they just could not defeat their enemies by sheer disadvantage of numbers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, historical factors also contribute to French society's great sense of comfort with allowing other people to look after their children.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I was told by French counterparts that already in the 19th century, women went to work.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When they went to work, someone had to look after the children.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: From those very early days, the beginning of the industrial revolution, they already had ideas that related to a creche or childcare.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, they have had a very long tradition.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Member is quite right that, by now, their childcare provision is very extensive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think this is also an aspiration that we will find within Singapore families.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think it is not just the women, as, very often, the husbands quite appreciate the fact that there are two sources of income.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It provides resources for the family that is more than one person can bring to bear.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We think that there are elements of that model that are worth us emulating.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to direct my clarification to Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo who mentioned that there will be a lot of support that is given in the period just before birth.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: And perhaps in the first, second year of pregnancy, I think the Government has done a wonderful job and I hope it will continue to do a good job in the area of providing that financial support.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: What about other support in the area of, say, services like counselling, and more support groups to even advise new parents on how to raise their children?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Currently, there is a plethora of such courses but they are expensive sometimes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: If you have the means, I know many young parents who have signed up for such courses.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: But parents from the lower-income groups may find it a bit prohibitive.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: So, would then Government please, either working with the grassroots or through other organisations, set up more support systems in the area of parenting classes, parenting workshops and so on, especially for new parents?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the answer is yes, we will certainly look into those.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If there are no other clarifications, Mr Ang Hin Kee, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: The Chairman
text: You do not need to thank the whole front bench.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
